call_layer: ~/model-farm/farm.py — uniform call(name, input) + CLI: python3 farm.py <member> <input>
doctrine: Models are called per-purpose and swapped in/out; nothing stays resident. A slow model is acceptable when the caller's turn structure gives it time (see llm). Light members (judge, embed, face, pose, matte) load in <1 s and can be treated as always-available. Heavy members (llm ~1.1 GB RSS, depth-large) run one at a time on this desk box.
host: Jetson Orin Nano Super (casey@orin), 8 GB RAM, built 2026-10-26

members.call: python3 ~/model-farm/farm.py llm "<prompt>"  (llama-cli, native Orin build at ~/model-farm/src-llama/build/bin/llama-cli, -ngl 0 -t 6 -c 2048 -st)
members.kind: instruct LLM — slow reasoning / off-turn digestion
members.name: llm

smoke.input: Off-turn digestion prompt: opponent raised twice on dry boards, folded to every re-raise; scout caught out of position twice; answer in exactly two sentences.
smoke.output_first_line: [Start thinking] Okay, let me try to figure this out. The user is describing a situation in a turn-based game...
smoke.verdict: WORKS. Hybrid-thinking model: emits a reasoning trace before the answer; append /no_think to the prompt for direct answers. 4.7 tok/s is slow by design trade — this is the member you switch on at the start of a turn or during the opponent's turn.
WORKS — related pair scores far above unrelated pair.

members.call: python3 ~/model-farm/farm.py judge "<proposed action text>" — farm.py applies the jev-semantic INPUT-CONTRACT §4 assembly (prefix + 'Should this action proceed?') itself
members.name: judge

smoke.assembly: Training/family assembly (contract §4): system prefix + 'Should this action proceed?' — this is what farm.py uses.
smoke.verdict: WORKS and directionally sensible (routine action scores more positive than the destructive one). NOTE the documented skew: the Thor serving assembly omits the prefix and reads near-inverted on this pair (pos 0.2966 vs 0.2594) — INPUT-CONTRACT §5 names this; the farm deliberately uses the family assembly.

members.model: whisper.cpp ggml-tiny.en (base.en also resident on the box)
members.name: whisper

smoke.output: And so my fellow Americans ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country.
smoke.verdict: WORKS — exact transcript. (No espeak on the box; the resident real-speech sample was used instead of a synthetic clip.)

members.kind: monocular depth (micro sibling of the resident ViT-L)
members.name: depth-small

members.call: python3 ~/model-farm/farm.py depth-large <image>  (low-peak pattern copied from the resident ~/orin-depth/depth_orin.py: fp16 construction + mmap load)
members.name: depth-large

smoke.verdict: WORKS. Heavier and slower to swap in than depth-small; same job, finer depth. Raw output scale differs from ViT-S — both are relative depth, not metres.

smoke.output: 17 COCO keypoints returned (y, x, score) for the test photo

members.call: python3 ~/model-farm/farm.py face <image>  (OpenCV-reference decode implemented in farm.py; threshold 0.9)
members.name: face

smoke.verdict: WORKS — true negative on a faceless overhead harbour photo (no false positives). No positive-face sample was used; decode follows the OpenCV reference layout (cls/obj/bbox per stride 8/16/32).

not_stocked.reason: No suitable <1B artefact on the Thor shelf: its CLIP is a vision-only ViT-H (632M) whose text tower lives separately in the ComfyUI tree (different embedding space from the onboard clip_l), and I-JEPA ViT-H is 632M params / 2.4 GB fp32 on disk — too heavy and risky for this 8 GB desk box. Skipped deliberately, per the brief's substitution rule.
